name: New York City
description: Eight million people packed onto a handful of islands, producing the densest concentration of culture, food, nightlife, and ambition on the planet. Every neighborhood is its own city — come for the icons, stay because you found your block.

identity.vibe: Relentless, electric, impossibly diverse — a city that rewards curiosity and punishes hesitation.

nexus_grid.title: Broadway & Entertainment
nexus_grid.description: The theater district alone draws 15M+ visitors annually — the single biggest tourism magnet in the city.

nexus_grid.title: World-Class Food Scene
nexus_grid.description: 70+ Michelin-starred restaurants, legendary pizza, every global cuisine represented — NYC is the food capital of the Western Hemisphere.

nexus_grid.title: Museums & Culture
nexus_grid.description: More world-class museums per square mile than anywhere on Earth — from the Met to hole-in-the-wall galleries in Chelsea.

modes.label: Foodie
modes.description: Every cuisine on Earth, from $1 pizza slices to three-Michelin-star tasting menus.

modes.label: Culture Vulture
modes.description: World-class museums, Broadway, galleries, historic landmarks, and the stories behind every block.

modes.label: Night Out
modes.description: Speakeasies, jazz clubs, comedy cellars, rooftop bars, and a 4am last call.

modes.label: Romantic
modes.description: Sunset bridge walks, candlelit restaurants, jazz in basement clubs, and skyline views.

modes.label: Family
modes.description: Dinosaurs at the museum, Central Park playgrounds, ferries, and Broadway matinees.

modes.label: Adventure
modes.description: Climb skyscrapers, walk bridges, explore five boroughs, and chase the unexpected.

modes.label: Chill
modes.description: Coffee shops, park benches, bookstores, and the art of watching the city go by.

modes.label: NYC on a Budget
modes.description: Free museums, dollar slices, park concerts, ferry rides, and the best things that cost nothing.

transit.local_transport: Subway runs 24/7 and goes nearly everywhere — it's the move. Uber/Lyft plentiful but expensive in traffic. Citi Bike for short trips. NYC Ferry connects waterfront neighborhoods for $4. Walking is the default. Do not rent a car unless you're leaving the city.

_legacy_transit.label: Drive
_legacy_transit.text: From anywhere — I-95 from the north/south, I-78/Holland Tunnel from NJ, I-495/Lincoln Tunnel from the west. Driving IN is easy. Parking is not.

_legacy_transit.label: Train
_legacy_transit.text: Amtrak Northeast Regional and Acela to Penn Station from DC (3.5h), Boston (3.5h), Philadelphia (1.5h). NJ Transit, Metro-North, LIRR for regional connections.

_legacy_transit.label: Fly
_legacy_transit.text: JFK International (Queens, ~1hr to Manhattan), LaGuardia (Queens, ~30-45min to Manhattan), Newark Liberty (NJ, ~1hr to Manhattan). JFK Terminal 6 Phase 1 reopening in 2026.

side_trips.name: Hudson Valley
side_trips.distance: 1.5-2 hours north by car or Metro-North
side_trips.pitch: The city's escape valve. River towns with farm-to-table restaurants, hiking trails, and fall foliage that looks like a painting.

side_trips.name: Fire Island
side_trips.distance: 2 hours east by LIRR + ferry (summer only)
side_trips.pitch: Car-free barrier island with pristine beaches, boardwalk communities, and a vibe that's half Provincetown, half summer camp.

side_trips.name: Asbury Park, NJ
side_trips.distance: 1.5 hours south by NJ Transit or car
side_trips.pitch: Bruce Springsteen's hometown, now a revitalized beach town with a killer food scene, indie shops, and live music venues.

side_trips.name: The Hamptons / Montauk
side_trips.distance: 2.5-3 hours east by LIRR or car
side_trips.pitch: The playground of Manhattan's elite — but Montauk at the tip feels more like a surf town than a socialite scene.

concierge.name: The Doorman
concierge.greeting: Welcome to the greatest city on Earth — and yeah, I've been everywhere else, and I'm still saying it. I'm The Doorman. I don't hold doors, I open them. What are you looking for?

_legacy.hero_title: New York City — Rooftops, Parks, and Sidewalk Everything
_legacy.hero_sub: The city spills outside. Shakespeare in the Park, rooftop bars from Brooklyn to Midtown, and the best people-watching on Earth. In 2026, FIFA World Cup matches and America 250 celebrations make this a once-in-a-generation summer.
